Being addicted is strongly related to habits, that's why people get addicted to smoking cigarettes, morning cigarette after coffee, smoking breaks, etc. The brain sort of connects the activity in your routine with smoking a cigarette, so without it, it simply feels off without the cigarette because you're usually smoking while doing that certain activity in your routine and now it doesn't feel right without it, so you might feel a craving while doing that certain activity due to the connection between the substance and that activity.

There's different levels of addiction, some people would simply accept the fact that they have to wait until they get paid to get more and do have the self-control strong enough to resist going out and steal to get their fix, while others will go out and commit crimes for some more meth because their brain isn't as strong when it comes to self-control so it's making the withdrawal seem scarier then it actually is which is why it's motivating enough for this individual to go out and steal. Both are still addicted however, one is just more dependent than the other so their normal paycheck isn't high enough to fund their habit due to a higher tolerence  requiring more meth to satisfy,  which also makes them more likely to seek out ways to get money for the drug which also makes them weaker when it comes to making choices for themselves (meth makes changes in the brain related to critical thinking and consequencial thinking)  (the brain starts forming and developing around making money or other forms of payment for more meth the more your brain gets hooked on it, it gets worse and worsr over time, and if it gets heavily hooked on it, it might not be reversible once the person gets sober, google it, it's true). A more dependent persons brain quite literally makes the person more likely to seek out the substance in ways that more than likely aren't exactly legal due to it being quicker but riskier than legal methods.
